title: The forecast
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, small snowbound American river town in deep winter, a vintage walnut shortwave radio with a warm amber dial glowing against cold blue night, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 4. Tonight the radio read her obituary. 🕯️

Original fiction. Part 5 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: Grandpa's notebook warned Lena that every change balances out, and the radio said her balance was due Friday.
scenes.image: a leather notebook lying open beside the glowing old radio on a kitchen table at night

scenes.narration: Wednesday night she sat in front of it with the notebook on her knee. At two minutes to midnight, the dial warmed like an eye opening.
scenes.image: woman sitting alone in a dark kitchen facing a glowing antique radio, notebook on her knee

scenes.narration: Weather first. Snow ending Thursday. Clear and bitter Friday night. A full moon over the river.
scenes.image: a full moon rising over a frozen river lined with bare black trees

scenes.narration: Then the voice softened, the way announcers do. And now, the obituaries.
scenes.image: extreme close-up of the radio's cloth speaker, amber glow, faint steam from a cup in the foreground

scenes.narration: Lena Marie Shaw, thirty-one, of Millbrook. Passed away Friday evening, at home. She is survived by her mother. And by a radio she should have left in the box.
scenes.image: woman's face frozen in shock, lit only by the amber glow of the radio dial

scenes.narration: She twisted the knob. Static. She twisted it back. The voice was still reading her life. Her high school. Her job at the pharmacy. Her grandfather, who went before her.
scenes.image: a trembling woman's hand gripping a brass radio knob in the dark

scenes.narration: In lieu of flowers, said the voice, the family asks that you stop listening.
scenes.image: the glowing radio in an otherwise black room, a woman standing several steps back from it

scenes.narration: Thursday, she called her mother. She didn't explain. She just said I love you, twice, and hung up before her voice broke.
scenes.image: woman on the phone beside a frosted window at dusk, eyes wet, hand over her mouth

scenes.narration: Thursday night, she swore she wouldn't listen. At two minutes to midnight, she was sitting in front of it again.
scenes.image: woman sitting on a kitchen floor hugging her knees, staring up at the glowing radio

scenes.narration: Same news. But after the sign-off, she heard breathing, close to the microphone. Then a whisper she knew from every bedtime of her childhood. Lena. Pull the plug.
scenes.image: extreme close-up of the radio dial glowing in darkness, a thin curl of pipe smoke drifting in front of it
